points.title: Iteration
points.model: Iteration (loop) = structure that repeats a block of statements. Count-controlled (for): known number of times, uses a counter. Condition-controlled (while, do…while): repeats while/until a condition is met; number of repetitions not known in advance.

points.title: Parts of a for loop
points.must: Initialisation (once), condition (before each pass), update (after each pass); counting the passes.
points.model: for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i++) { … }: initialisation let i = 1 runs once; condition i <= 5 checked before every pass; update i++ after every pass. i = 1..5 → 5 passes; stops when i = 6. for (i = 10; i >= 0; i -= 4) → 10, 6, 2 → 3 passes.

points.title: while vs do … while
points.must: Pre-condition: tested first, 0 or more times; post-condition: tested after, at least once; use for input validation.
points.model: while = pre-condition loop: condition tested before the body → may run 0 times. do … while = post-condition loop: body first, then test → runs at least once. Input check: do { mark = Number(prompt(…)); } while (isNaN(mark) || mark < 0 || mark > 100);

points.title: Choosing a loop
points.must: Known count → for/foreach; unknown + at least once → do…while; otherwise while; comparison table PHP/JS.
points.model: Known number → for (foreach / for…of for arrays: foreach ($marks as $m)). Unknown, must run at least once → do…while. Unknown, may be 0 times → while.

points.title: Totals and counters
points.must: Initialise before the loop; total += value; counter++; PHP average example.
points.model: Set total = 0 and count = 0 BEFORE the loop. $marks = [7, 9, 4, 10]; foreach: $total += $m → 30; average = 30 / count($marks) = 7.5.

points.title: break and infinite loops
points.must: break leaves the loop; infinite loop when the condition variable never changes; 3-attempt PIN code.
points.model: break = leave the loop at once; continue = skip to next pass. Infinite loop: condition never becomes false (e.g. attempts++ missing). PIN: while (attempts < 3) { pin = prompt(); attempts++; if (pin == "1234") { success = true; break; } } then if (success) … else "Card blocked".

points.title: Trace table
points.must: Method (column per variable, row per check) + example total of 1,3,5,7 = 16 and while loop until 150 000 ₸ = 4 years.
points.model: Column for each variable + condition, one row per check. for (i = 1; i <= 7; i += 2) total += i: i 1,3,5,7 → total 1,4,9,16; i = 9 false → output 16. Savings 100 000 × 1.14 until ≥ 150 000 → 4 years.

points.title: Nested loops
points.must: Inner loop runs fully for each outer pass; 3 × 4 = 12; rows and seats example.
points.model: Inner loop completes for every outer iteration: 3 rows × 4 seats = 12 passes → A1 A2 A3 A4 B1 … Used for tables, 2D arrays.

points.title: Validation
points.must: Definition: automatic check by the program that data is sensible / follows rules; cannot check correctness.
points.model: Validation = automatic check by the program that data is reasonable/sensible and follows the rules before it is accepted. It checks data is allowed, not that it is correct (age 17 instead of 16 passes).

points.title: Verification
points.must: Definition: data entered/copied accurately, matches original; double entry, visual check; comparison with validation.
points.model: Verification = check that data was entered/copied accurately and matches the original. Methods: double entry (type twice and compare: if (pass !== confirm)), visual check / proof-reading. Validation asks "is it allowed?", verification "is it what was meant?".

points.title: Validation checks in code
points.must: Presence, length, type, range, format, lookup with JS (and PHP) code; check digit.
points.model: Presence: name === ""; Length: password.length < 8 / strlen(); Type: isNaN(age) / !is_numeric(); Range: age < 14 || age > 18; Format: /^\d{6}$/.test(postcode), filter_var(email, FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL); Lookup: ["A","B","C"].includes(grade) / in_array(). Check digit: last digit calculated from the others (ISBN, card numbers). Type check before range check.

points.title: Validate on client and server
points.must: Client: instant feedback, preventDefault; server: client checks can be bypassed; two-layer flow.
points.model: JS (HTML required/min/max/pattern) → instant feedback, less server load; event.preventDefault() stops sending. PHP repeats every check because client-side checks can be switched off or bypassed (data sent directly).

points.title: Olympiad form example and test data
points.must: Check for each field + normal, boundary, erroneous test data.
points.model: Surname presence; grade lookup 9/10/11; IIN format /^\d{12}$/; year range 2006–2012; email typed twice = verification. Test: normal 2009, boundary 2006 & 2012 (accept), 2005 & 2013 (reject), erroneous "two thousand".

points.title: Good programming style
points.must: At least five rules: meaningful identifiers, indentation, comments, constants, functions, validation; why.
points.model: Meaningful identifiers (totalCost not x); consistent naming (camelCase); indentation of if/loop bodies; one statement per line; comments explain why; constants instead of magic numbers (const MAX_ATTEMPTS = 3); functions with one job; validate input and handle errors. → easier to read, test, fix.
